blurb.en: From the garden where it all began to the empty tomb: meet the God who made you, rescues you and calls you His child.
blurb.af: Van die tuin waar alles begin het tot by die leë graf: leer die God ken wat jou gemaak het, jou red en jou sy kind noem.

blurb.en: Where it all begins: God who made the stars, the lions and you.
blurb.af: Waar alles begin: God wat die sterre, die leeus en jou gemaak het.

en.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

af.text: In die begin het God die hemel en die aarde geskep.

en.title: The Biggest Build Ever
story: Long, long ago, before there were trees or puppies or even the sun, there was nothing at all. Nothing… except God. God has always been there.

Then God spoke. ‘Let there be light!’ And WHOOSH! Light burst out everywhere. Day by day God kept building. He made the sky and the deep blue sea. He made mountains to climb and trees to swing in. He hung the sun up to warm the day, and scattered the stars across the night like glitter.
Then God filled his world with life: fish that splash, birds that swoop, lions that ROAR and tiny ants that march. God looked at everything he had made and smiled. ‘It is very good!’
Every time you see a sunset, a beetle or a big wave, you are looking at something God made with his own great imagination.

verse.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

lessons: God made everything, even the stars too far away to see.
God is powerful: he only had to speak!
God is creative. He loves making beautiful things.
questions: What is your favourite thing that God made?
If you could ask God how he made something, what would you ask?
prayer: Dear God,
you made the sky and the sea,
the lions and the stars.
Thank you for your beautiful world.
You are amazing! Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, find one thing outside that God made and say, ‘Thank you, God, for the ___!’

af.title: Die Grootste Bouwerk Ooit
story: Lank, lank gelede, voordat daar bome of hondjies of selfs die son was, was daar niks nie. Niks… behalwe God. God was nog altyd daar.

Toe het God gepraat. ‘Laat daar lig wees!’ En WOESJ! Lig het oral uitgebars. Dag na dag het God verder gebou. Hy het die lug en die diep blou see gemaak. Hy het berge gemaak om op te klim en bome om in te swaai. Hy het die son opgehang om die dag warm te maak, en die sterre soos glitter oor die nag gestrooi.
Toe het God sy wêreld vol lewe gemaak: visse wat spat, voëls wat swiep, leeus wat BRUL en klein miertjies wat marsjeer. God het na alles gekyk wat Hy gemaak het en geglimlag. ‘Dit is baie goed!’
Elke keer as jy ’n sonsondergang, ’n kewer of ’n groot golf sien, kyk jy na iets wat God met sy groot verbeelding gemaak het.

verse.text: In die begin het God die hemel en die aarde geskep.

lessons: God het alles gemaak, selfs die sterre wat te ver is om te sien.
God is sterk: Hy moes net praat!
God is kreatief. Hy hou daarvan om mooi dinge te maak.
questions: Wat is jou gunstelingding wat God gemaak het?
As jy vir God kon vra hoe Hy iets gemaak het, wat sou jy vra?
prayer: Liewe God,
U het die lug en die see gemaak,
die leeus en die sterre.
Dankie vir u mooi wêreld.
U is wonderlik! Amen.

mission.text: Soek môre een ding buite wat God gemaak het en sê: ‘Dankie, God, vir die ___!’

en.title: God Made Everything
story: A long, long time ago there was nothing at all. Only God.
God spoke, and the light came on! Whoosh!
God made the sky so blue and the sea so big. He made the sun for the day and the stars for the night.
God made fish that swim, birds that fly and lions that ROAR!
God looked at everything and smiled. ‘It is very good!’

verse.text: God made everything.

en.action: Make a big circle with your arms for the whole world. Then flap like a bird, swim like a fish and roar like a lion!
lessons: God made everything, and He made it good.
questions: Can you point to something God made?
prayer: Thank you, God,
for making everything. Amen.

af.title: God Het Alles Gemaak
story: Lank, lank gelede was daar niks nie. Net God.
God het gepraat, en die lig het aangegaan! Woesj!
God het die lug so blou gemaak en die see so groot. Hy het die son vir die dag gemaak en die sterre vir die nag.
God het visse gemaak wat swem, voëls wat vlieg en leeus wat BRUL!
God het na alles gekyk en geglimlag. ‘Dit is baie goed!’

verse.text: God het alles gemaak.

af.action: Maak ’n groot sirkel met jou arms vir die hele wêreld. Klap dan jou vlerke soos ’n voël, swem soos ’n vis en brul soos ’n leeu!
lessons: God het alles gemaak, en Hy het dit goed gemaak.
questions: Kan jy wys na iets wat God gemaak het?
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U alles gemaak het. Amen.

en.title: In the Beginning
story: Before there was a single atom in the universe, before time even started ticking, there was God. Nobody made God. He has always been there: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, perfectly happy together.

Then God decided to create. Genesis says, ‘God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.’ Notice what God used to build the universe: words. He didn’t need tools or materials. He simply spoke, and things that did not exist came into being. Light. Sky. Oceans. Dry land. Plants with seeds inside them, so they could make more plants.

On day four God placed the sun, the moon and billions of stars in the sky. On day five He filled the seas with fish and the air with birds. On day six He made animals of every kind, from elephants to earthworms. Scientists are still discovering creatures God made that nobody has ever seen before.

Then God did something different. He made people, and He made them ‘in His image’. That means people are like God in a special way: we can think, create, love, choose and talk with Him. No other creature was made like that. God made people to be His children and to look after His world with Him.
At the end of the sixth day God looked at everything He had made and said it was ‘very good’. On the seventh day He rested, not because He was tired, but to enjoy what He had made.

Here is the amazing part: the same voice that spoke the stars into being still speaks today. God speaks through the Bible, and by His Spirit He speaks to the hearts of His children. The God who made the universe wants to talk with you.

verse.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

lessons: God is the Creator. Everything that exists, He made, and He made it good.
God made people in His image, to be His children and to know Him.
God’s words are powerful. The voice that created the world still speaks today.
questions: What did God use to create the world? Why is that amazing?
What does it mean that you are made ‘in God’s image’?
Where did you see something God made today? What does it tell you about Him?
en.listen: Sit quietly for one minute. Think about something beautiful God made. Ask Him: ‘God, what do you want me to know about you tonight?’ If a kind thought comes, write it down or tell your parent. God’s voice always agrees with the Bible and sounds like love.
prayer: God, you are the Creator of everything.
Thank you for making me in your image.
Tonight I want to thank you for…

mission.text: Go on a ‘creation hunt’ tomorrow: find five things God made and thank Him for each one.

en.journal: Draw or write about your favourite part of creation. What does it show you about what God is like?

af.title: In die Begin
story: Voordat daar ’n enkele atoom in die heelal was, voordat tyd selfs begin tik het, was daar God. Niemand het God gemaak nie. Hy was nog altyd daar: Vader, Seun en Heilige Gees, volkome gelukkig saam.

Toe het God besluit om te skep. Genesis sê: ‘God het gesê: “Laat daar lig wees!” En daar was lig.’ Let op wat God gebruik het om die heelal te bou: woorde. Hy het nie gereedskap of materiaal nodig gehad nie. Hy het net gepraat, en dinge wat nie bestaan het nie, het ontstaan. Lig. Lug. Oseane. Droë grond. Plante met sade in, sodat hulle meer plante kon maak.

Op dag vier het God die son, die maan en biljoene sterre in die hemel gesit. Op dag vyf het Hy die see vol visse en die lug vol voëls gemaak. Op dag ses het Hy allerhande diere gemaak, van olifante tot erdwurms. Wetenskaplikes ontdek steeds diere wat God gemaak het wat nog niemand ooit gesien het nie.

Toe het God iets anders gedoen. Hy het mense gemaak, en Hy het hulle ‘na sy beeld’ gemaak. Dit beteken mense is op ’n spesiale manier soos God: ons kan dink, skep, liefhê, kies en met Hom praat. Geen ander skepsel is so gemaak nie. God het mense gemaak om sy kinders te wees en saam met Hom na sy wêreld om te sien.
Aan die einde van die sesde dag het God na alles gekyk wat Hy gemaak het en gesê dit is ‘baie goed’. Op die sewende dag het Hy gerus, nie omdat Hy moeg was nie, maar om te geniet wat Hy gemaak het.

Hier is die wonderlike deel: dieselfde stem wat die sterre laat ontstaan het, praat vandag nog. God praat deur die Bybel, en deur sy Gees praat Hy met die harte van sy kinders. Die God wat die heelal gemaak het, wil met jou praat.

verse.text: In die begin het God die hemel en die aarde geskep.

lessons: God is die Skepper. Alles wat bestaan, het Hy gemaak, en Hy het dit goed gemaak.
God het mense na sy beeld gemaak, om sy kinders te wees en Hom te ken.
God se woorde is kragtig. Die stem wat die wêreld geskep het, praat vandag nog.
questions: Wat het God gebruik om die wêreld te skep? Hoekom is dit wonderlik?
Wat beteken dit dat jy ‘na God se beeld’ gemaak is?
Waar het jy vandag iets gesien wat God gemaak het? Wat sê dit vir jou oor Hom?
af.listen: Sit een minuut lank stil. Dink aan iets moois wat God gemaak het. Vra Hom: ‘God, wat wil U hê moet ek vanaand oor U weet?’ As ’n liefdevolle gedagte kom, skryf dit neer of vertel jou ouer. God se stem stem altyd ooreen met die Bybel en klink na liefde.
prayer: God, U is die Skepper van alles.
Dankie dat U my na u beeld gemaak het.
Vanaand wil ek U dankie sê vir…

mission.text: Gaan môre op ’n ‘skeppingsjag’: soek vyf dinge wat God gemaak het en sê vir elkeen dankie.

af.journal: Teken of skryf oor jou gunstelingdeel van die skepping. Wat wys dit vir jou oor hoe God is?

trait.en: God is the Creator
trait.af: God is die Skepper

en.title: Made by God's Hands
story: At the end of making everything, God saved the best for last. He scooped up dust from the ground and shaped it carefully, like you shape playdough. Then God breathed into it, and the first man, Adam, opened his eyes and took a big breath! Later God made Eve, the first woman.
People were different from everything else God made. God made people to be a little bit like him: to think, to love, to laugh, to make things, and to be his very own children, close to him.

And here is something wonderful: God made YOU too. He chose your eyes and your smile and the way you laugh. He knew you before you were even born. There is no one else in the whole world exactly like you, and God thinks you are wonderful.

verse.text: I praise you because you made me in an amazing and wonderful way.

lessons: God made you on purpose. You are not an accident.
God made people to be his children, close to him.
Because God made everyone, every person is special to him.
questions: What is something God gave you that you love? (Hands that build? Legs that run?)
Who is someone else God made special?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for making me.
Thank you for my hands, my feet and my smile.
Help me remember I am yours. Amen.

mission.text: Tell someone in your family one thing that makes them special.

af.title: Deur God se Hande Gemaak
story: Aan die einde van alles het God die beste vir laaste gehou. Hy het stof van die grond opgeskep en dit versigtig gevorm, soos jy klei vorm. Toe het God daarin geblaas, en die eerste man, Adam, het sy oë oopgemaak en ’n groot asem gehaal! Later het God Eva gemaak, die eerste vrou.
Mense was anders as alles wat God gemaak het. God het mense ’n bietjie soos Hy gemaak: om te dink, lief te hê, te lag, dinge te maak, en om sy eie kinders te wees, naby aan Hom.

En hier is iets wonderliks: God het JOU ook gemaak. Hy het jou oë en jou glimlag gekies en die manier waarop jy lag. Hy het jou geken nog voordat jy gebore is. Daar is niemand anders in die hele wêreld presies soos jy nie, en God dink jy is wonderlik.

verse.text: Ek loof U, want U het my wonderlik en mooi gemaak.

lessons: God het jou met ’n doel gemaak. Jy is nie ’n ongeluk nie.
God het mense gemaak om sy kinders te wees, naby aan Hom.
Omdat God almal gemaak het, is elke mens spesiaal vir Hom.
questions: Wat het God vir jou gegee waarvoor jy baie lief is? (Hande wat bou? Bene wat hardloop?)
Wie is iemand anders wat God spesiaal gemaak het?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U my gemaak het.
Dankie vir my hande, my voete en my glimlag.
Help my om te onthou ek is u kind. Amen.

mission.text: Sê môre vir iemand in jou familie een ding wat hulle spesiaal maak.

af.deeper: As God jou met ’n doel gemaak het, hoe kan dit jou help op ’n dag wanneer jy voel jy is nie goed genoeg nie?

en.title: God Made Me
story: God made the trees and the flowers and the animals.
Then God made people. He made them like Him, so they could love and laugh and be His children.
And God made YOU! He made your eyes, your nose and your toes. Wiggle them!
God loves you so much. You are His child.

verse.text: God made me wonderful.

en.action: Touch your eyes, your nose and your toes, and say: ‘God made me!’
lessons: God made me, and He loves me. I am His child.
questions: What did God give you? Can you show me your hands?
prayer: Thank you, God,
for making me. I love you. Amen.

af.title: God Het My Gemaak
story: God het die bome en die blomme en die diere gemaak.
Toe het God mense gemaak. Hy het hulle soos Hy gemaak, sodat hulle kon liefhê en lag en sy kinders kon wees.
En God het JOU gemaak! Hy het jou oë, jou neus en jou tone gemaak. Wikkel hulle!
God is so lief vir jou. Jy is sy kind.

verse.text: God het my wonderlik gemaak.

af.action: Raak aan jou oë, jou neus en jou tone, en sê: ‘God het my gemaak!’
lessons: God het my gemaak, en Hy is lief vir my. Ek is sy kind.
questions: Wat het God vir jou gegee? Kan jy vir my jou hande wys?
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U my gemaak het. Ek is lief vir U. Amen.

en.title: Knitted Together
story: Genesis 2 zooms in on day six and shows us how God made the first man. God took dust from the ground and formed it, the way a potter shapes clay. Then God breathed into the man’s nostrils, and Adam became a living person. Every breath you take tonight is a gift from that same God.

God planted a garden in Eden and put Adam there to look after it. Adam named all the animals. That was a big job, and it shows that God trusted people with real responsibility. But among all the animals there was no one like Adam. So God made Eve, the first woman, and brought her to Adam. Now there were people to share life with.

Hundreds of years later King David thought about how God makes every person. He wrote Psalm 139: ‘You created my inmost being; you knit me together in my mother’s womb.’ Knitting is slow, careful work. David was saying that God made him on purpose, stitch by stitch.

That is true of you too. God chose the colour of your eyes, the sound of your laugh and the things you are good at. He knew you before you were born, and He wrote down all your days. There has never been another you, and there never will be.
Being made by God means you belong to Him. You are not an accident, and you don’t have to earn your worth. God made you to be His child, and He delights in you.

verse.text: I praise you because you made me in an amazing and wonderful way.

lessons: God made every person on purpose, carefully and lovingly.
God made people to be His children and gave them important work to do.
My worth comes from the God who made me, not from what I do or what others think.
questions: How did God make Adam? What did He breathe into him?
Why do you think David compared God’s work to knitting?
When do you feel ‘not good enough’? What does Psalm 139 say to you then?
en.listen: Be still for one minute. Ask God: ‘What do you think about me?’ Listen. God’s words to you will always be kind and true, like the words of Psalm 139.
prayer: Father, thank you for making me on purpose.
Help me to believe what you say about me.
Thank you that I am your child.

mission.text: God made every person carefully. Tomorrow, tell three people something you appreciate about them.

en.journal: Write ‘God made me’ in the middle of a page. Around it, write or draw ten things God gave you.

af.title: Saamgebrei
story: Genesis 2 zoem in op dag ses en wys ons hoe God die eerste man gemaak het. God het stof van die grond geneem en dit gevorm, soos ’n pottebakker klei vorm. Toe het God in die man se neus geblaas, en Adam het ’n lewende mens geword. Elke asem wat jy vanaand haal, is ’n geskenk van daardie selfde God.

God het ’n tuin in Eden geplant en Adam daar gesit om dit op te pas. Adam het al die diere name gegee. Dit was ’n groot werk, en dit wys dat God mense met regte verantwoordelikheid vertrou het. Maar tussen al die diere was daar niemand soos Adam nie. Toe het God Eva gemaak, die eerste vrou, en haar na Adam gebring. Nou was daar mense om die lewe mee te deel.

Honderde jare later het koning Dawid gedink oor hoe God elke mens maak. Hy het Psalm 139 geskryf: ‘U het my binneste gevorm; U het my in my ma se skoot saamgebrei.’ Brei is stadige, versigtige werk. Dawid het gesê dat God hom met ’n doel gemaak het, steek vir steek.

Dit is ook waar van jou. God het die kleur van jou oë gekies, die klank van jou lag en die dinge waarin jy goed is. Hy het jou geken voordat jy gebore is, en Hy het al jou dae neergeskryf. Daar was nog nooit ’n ander jy nie, en daar sal ook nooit wees nie.
Omdat God jou gemaak het, behoort jy aan Hom. Jy is nie ’n ongeluk nie, en jy hoef nie jou waarde te verdien nie. God het jou gemaak om sy kind te wees, en Hy het vreugde in jou.

verse.text: Ek loof U, want U het my wonderlik en mooi gemaak.

lessons: God het elke mens met ’n doel gemaak, versigtig en liefdevol.
God het mense gemaak om sy kinders te wees en het hulle belangrike werk gegee.
My waarde kom van die God wat my gemaak het, nie van wat ek doen of wat ander dink nie.
questions: Hoe het God Adam gemaak? Wat het Hy in hom geblaas?
Hoekom dink jy het Dawid God se werk met brei vergelyk?
Wanneer voel jy ‘nie goed genoeg nie’? Wat sê Psalm 139 dan vir jou?
af.listen: Wees een minuut lank stil. Vra God: ‘Wat dink U van my?’ Luister. God se woorde vir jou sal altyd liefdevol en waar wees, soos die woorde van Psalm 139.
prayer: Vader, dankie dat U my met ’n doel gemaak het.
Help my om te glo wat U oor my sê.
Dankie dat ek u kind is.

mission.text: God het elke mens versigtig gemaak. Sê môre vir drie mense iets wat jy in hulle waardeer.

en.title: Where Are You?
story: God put Adam and Eve in a beautiful garden called Eden. In the cool of the evening, God came walking in the garden to spend time with them. Imagine going for a walk with God!

God gave them only one rule: ‘Don’t eat from that one tree.’ But a sneaky snake whispered, ‘Go on. God doesn’t really want what’s best for you.’ Eve ate the fruit, and Adam did too. Suddenly they felt sad and scared, and they hid behind the bushes.
Then they heard God calling: ‘Where are you?’ God already knew where they were. He was calling because he still wanted to be with them.

Disobeying God (we call it sin) spoiled their closeness with God, their loving Father, and things had to change. But that very same day God made a promise: one day he would send a Rescuer to fix everything. Can you guess who that Rescuer is? Jesus!

verse.text: But the Lord God called to the man, ‘Where are you?’

lessons: God wants to be close to us. He even went walking with Adam and Eve.
When we do wrong, we want to hide, but God comes looking for us.
God had a rescue plan from the very beginning: Jesus.
questions: How do you feel inside when you have done something wrong?
What can we do instead of hiding? (Tell God and say sorry.)
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you always come looking for me.
When I do wrong, help me not to hide.
Help me run to you and say sorry. Amen.

mission.text: If you do something wrong tomorrow, don’t hide it. Say sorry to God and to the person.

en.title: Where Are You?
story: God made a beautiful garden for Adam and Eve.
God said, ‘Don’t eat from that one tree.’ But they did. Oh no!
They felt sad, and they hid behind a bush.
But God came looking. ‘Where are you?’ God still loved them.
And God made a promise: one day He would send Jesus to make everything right.

verse.text: God called, ‘Where are you?’

en.action: Play peekaboo! Hide behind your hands, then pop out: ‘Here I am!’ God always comes looking for us.
lessons: When I do wrong, God still loves me. I can say sorry.
questions: What can we say when we do something wrong? (Sorry!)
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you always find me. Amen.

af.title: Waar Is Jy?
story: God het ’n pragtige tuin vir Adam en Eva gemaak.
God het gesê: ‘Moenie van daardie een boom eet nie.’ Maar hulle het. O nee!
Hulle was hartseer, en hulle het agter ’n bos weggekruip.
Maar God het kom soek. ‘Waar is jy?’ God was nog steeds lief vir hulle.
En God het ’n belofte gemaak: eendag sou Hy Jesus stuur om alles reg te maak.

verse.text: God het geroep: ‘Waar is jy?’

af.action: Speel kiekeboe! Kruip agter jou hande weg, en spring dan uit: ‘Hier is ek!’ God kom altyd na ons soek.
lessons: As ek iets verkeerd doen, is God nog steeds lief vir my. Ek kan jammer sê.
questions: Wat kan ons sê as ons iets verkeerd gedoen het? (Jammer!)
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U my altyd kry. Amen.

en.title: The Hiding and the Seeking
story: Life in the garden was perfect. Adam and Eve walked with God, talked with Him and had everything they needed. God had given them one rule: don’t eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. If they did, He warned, they would die.

One day the serpent (the Bible later tells us this was Satan) asked Eve a sneaky question: ‘Did God really say…?’ Then he told a lie: ‘You won’t die. God just doesn’t want you to be like Him.’ The lie made God sound mean and unfair. Eve looked at the fruit, took some and ate it. Adam ate it too.
Immediately everything changed. For the first time they felt shame. They sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves, and when they heard God walking in the garden, they hid among the trees.

This is what the Bible calls sin: choosing our own way instead of God’s way. Sin brought death into the world: our bodies would one day die, and people were cut off from God. From that day on, every person has been born with a heart that leans toward sin. That is why nobody has to teach a toddler to grab or to shout ‘Mine!’

But look what God did next. He came looking. ‘Where are you?’ He already knew where they were. He was inviting them to come out of hiding. There were consequences, and life outside the garden would be hard. But God also made a promise. Genesis 3:15 says one of Eve’s descendants would crush the serpent’s head. This is the very first promise in the Bible about Jesus, who would one day defeat sin and Satan on the cross.
When you do something wrong, you might want to hide too. But God is still the One who comes looking. Because of Jesus, you can come out of hiding, tell God the truth and be forgiven.

verse.text: But the Lord God called to the man, ‘Where are you?’

lessons: Sin is choosing our own way instead of God’s way, and every person has sin in their heart.
Sin makes us want to hide from God, but God comes looking for us.
From the very beginning, God promised a Rescuer: Jesus.
questions: What lie did the serpent tell about God?
Why did Adam and Eve hide? Why did God call out to them?
What do you usually do when you’ve done something wrong? What could you do instead?
en.listen: Be quiet for one minute. Ask God: ‘Is there anything I need to bring out of hiding?’ If something comes to mind, tell God about it and say sorry. Then listen again: what does He say to you? (Hint: read 1 John 1:9.)
prayer: God, thank you that you came looking for Adam and Eve, and you come looking for me.
I’m sorry for…
Thank you for Jesus, the Rescuer you promised.

mission.text: If you get something wrong tomorrow, don’t hide it. Tell God and the person, and say sorry.

en.journal: Write Genesis 3:15 in your own words. Why do you think God made this promise on the same day Adam and Eve sinned?

af.title: Wegkruip en Soek
story: Die lewe in die tuin was volmaak. Adam en Eva het saam met God gewandel, met Hom gepraat en alles gehad wat hulle nodig gehad het. God het hulle een reël gegee: moenie van die boom van die kennis van goed en kwaad eet nie. As hulle dit doen, het Hy gewaarsku, sal hulle sterf.

Eendag het die slang (die Bybel vertel ons later dat dit Satan was) vir Eva ’n skelm vraag gevra: ‘Het God regtig gesê…?’ Toe het hy ’n leuen vertel: ‘Julle sal nie sterf nie. God wil net nie hê julle moet soos Hy wees nie.’ Die leuen het God gemeen en onregverdig laat klink. Eva het na die vrug gekyk, daarvan gevat en geëet. Adam het ook geëet.

Dadelik het alles verander. Vir die eerste keer het hulle skaam gevoel. Hulle het vyeblare aanmekaargewerk om hulself te bedek, en toe hulle God in die tuin hoor loop, het hulle tussen die bome weggekruip.

Dit is wat die Bybel sonde noem: om ons eie pad te kies in plaas van God se pad. Sonde het die dood in die wêreld gebring: ons liggame sou eendag sterf, en mense is van God afgesny. Van daardie dag af word elke mens gebore met ’n hart wat na sonde toe neig. Dit is hoekom niemand ’n kleuter hoef te leer om te gryp of ‘Myne!’ te skree nie.

Maar kyk wat God toe gedoen het. Hy het kom soek. ‘Waar is jy?’ Hy het klaar geweet waar hulle was. Hy het hulle uitgenooi om uit hulle wegkruipplek te kom. Daar was gevolge, en die lewe buite die tuin sou moeilik wees. Maar God het ook ’n belofte gemaak. Genesis 3:15 sê een van Eva se nakomelinge sal die slang se kop vermorsel. Dit is die heel eerste belofte in die Bybel oor Jesus, wat eendag sonde en Satan aan die kruis sou oorwin.
As jy iets verkeerd doen, wil jy dalk ook wegkruip. Maar God is steeds die Een wat kom soek. Danksy Jesus kan jy uit jou wegkruipplek kom, die waarheid vir God vertel en vergewe word.

verse.text: Maar die Here God het na die man geroep: ‘Waar is jy?’

lessons: Sonde is om ons eie pad te kies in plaas van God se pad, en elke mens het sonde in sy of haar hart.
Sonde laat ons van God wil wegkruip, maar God kom soek na ons.
Van die heel begin af het God ’n Redder belowe: Jesus.
questions: Watter leuen het die slang oor God vertel?
Hoekom het Adam en Eva weggekruip? Hoekom het God na hulle geroep?
Wat doen jy gewoonlik as jy iets verkeerd gedoen het? Wat kan jy eerder doen?
af.listen: Wees een minuut lank stil. Vra God: ‘Is daar iets wat ek uit my wegkruipplek moet bring?’ As iets opkom, vertel God daarvan en sê jammer. Luister dan weer: wat sê Hy vir jou? (Wenk: lees 1 Johannes 1:9.)
prayer: God, dankie dat U na Adam en Eva kom soek het, en dat U na my kom soek.
Ek is jammer vir…
Dankie vir Jesus, die Redder wat U belowe het.

mission.text: As jy môre iets verkeerd doen, moenie dit wegsteek nie. Vertel God en die persoon, en sê jammer.

af.journal: Skryf Genesis 3:15 in jou eie woorde. Hoekom dink jy het God hierdie belofte gemaak op dieselfde dag wat Adam en Eva gesondig het?

trait.en: God loves me even when I get it wrong
trait.af: God het my lief, selfs as ek iets verkeerd doen

en.title: The Big Boat and the Rainbow
story: Many years later, people had forgotten God. They were mean and hurt each other, and it made God’s heart very sad. But one man, Noah, still loved God and listened to him.

God told Noah, ‘Build a giant boat, an ark!’ Noah had never seen a flood, but he trusted God. Bang, bang, bang went his hammer, for years and years! Then the animals came, two by two: elephants stomping, monkeys chattering, giraffes ducking their heads to fit through the door.

Then the rain came. It rained and rained for forty days and forty nights, until water covered the whole earth. But inside the ark, Noah, his family and the animals were safe, because God was looking after them.

When the water finally went down, God put a beautiful rainbow in the sky. ‘This is my promise,’ God said. ‘I will never flood the whole earth again.’ And God has kept that promise every single day since.

verse.text: I have put my rainbow in the clouds. It is the sign of my promise.

lessons: God always keeps his promises.
God takes care of people who trust him, even in storms.
Noah obeyed God even when it seemed strange.
questions: When you see a rainbow, what can it remind you of?
Has someone ever made you a promise and kept it? How did it feel?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you always keep your promises.
When I see a rainbow,
help me remember you are faithful. Amen.

mission.text: Make a promise to someone tomorrow (like ‘I will help tidy up’) and keep it, just like God does.

af.title: Die Groot Boot en die Reënboog
story: Baie jare later het mense van God vergeet. Hulle was gemeen en het mekaar seergemaak, en dit het God se hart baie hartseer gemaak. Maar een man, Noag, was nog lief vir God en het na Hom geluister.

God het vir Noag gesê: ‘Bou ’n reusagtige boot, ’n ark!’ Noag het nog nooit ’n vloed gesien nie, maar hy het God vertrou. Klop, klop, klop het sy hamer gegaan, jare en jare lank! Toe het die diere gekom, twee-twee: olifante wat stamp, ape wat babbel, kameelperde wat hul koppe moes buk om deur die deur te kom.

Toe kom die reën. Dit het gereën en gereën, veertig dae en veertig nagte lank, totdat water die hele aarde bedek het. Maar binne-in die ark was Noag, sy familie en die diere veilig, want God het na hulle gekyk.

Toe die water eindelik gesak het, het God ’n pragtige reënboog in die lug gesit. ‘Dit is my belofte,’ het God gesê. ‘Ek sal nooit weer die hele aarde laat oorstroom nie.’ En God het daardie belofte elke enkele dag gehou.

verse.text: Ek het my reënboog in die wolke gesit. Dit is die teken van my belofte.

lessons: God hou altyd sy beloftes.
God sorg vir mense wat Hom vertrou, selfs in storms.
Noag was gehoorsaam aan God, selfs toe dit vreemd gelyk het.
questions: As jy ’n reënboog sien, waaraan kan dit jou herinner?
Het iemand al ooit vir jou ’n belofte gemaak en dit gehou? Hoe het dit gevoel?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U altyd u beloftes hou.
As ek ’n reënboog sien,
help my om te onthou U is getrou. Amen.

mission.text: Maak môre ’n belofte aan iemand (soos ‘Ek sal help opruim’) en hou dit, net soos God doen.

en.title: Noah’s Big Boat
story: Noah loved God.
God said, ‘Build a big, big boat!’ Bang, bang, bang went Noah’s hammer.
Then the animals came, two by two. Elephants, giraffes, and little ducks too!
Pitter-patter, the rain came down. But Noah and the animals were safe inside.
Then God put a rainbow in the sky. ‘I always keep my promises,’ said God.

verse.text: God keeps His promises.

en.action: Bang a hammer with your fist, make pitter-patter rain with your fingers, then draw a big rainbow in the air.
lessons: God always keeps His promises.
questions: Which animal would you take on the boat? What sound does it make?
prayer: Thank you, God,
that you keep me safe. Amen.

af.title: Noag se Groot Boot
story: Noag was lief vir God.
God het gesê: ‘Bou ’n groot, groot boot!’ Klop, klop, klop het Noag se hamer gegaan.
Toe het die diere gekom, twee-twee. Olifante, kameelperde, en klein eendjies ook!
Tik-tik-tik het die reën geval. Maar Noag en die diere was veilig binne-in.
Toe het God ’n reënboog in die lug gesit. ‘Ek hou altyd my beloftes,’ het God gesê.

af.action: Kap ’n hamer met jou vuis, maak tik-tik-reën met jou vingers, en teken dan ’n groot reënboog in die lug.
lessons: God hou altyd sy beloftes.
questions: Watter dier sou jy op die boot saamneem? Watter geluid maak dit?
prayer: Dankie, God,
dat U my veilig hou. Amen.

en.title: The Ark and the Rainbow
story: By Noah’s time the world had become a terrible place. The Bible says people’s thoughts were ‘only evil all the time’. Violence was everywhere. It grieved God, which means it hurt His heart, that the people He had made had turned so far from Him.

But Noah ‘found favour in the eyes of the Lord’. Noah walked with God. So God told Noah His plan: a flood would cover the earth, but Noah, his family and two of every kind of animal would be kept safe in an enormous boat called an ark. God gave exact measurements: about 135 metres long, 22 metres wide and 13 metres high.

The Bible says, ‘Noah did everything just as God commanded him.’ Building the ark took years. There was no rain in sight, and people must have thought Noah had lost his mind. But Noah trusted what God said more than what he could see. That is what faith is.
When the flood came, it rained for forty days and forty nights, and the water covered even the mountains. But inside the ark everyone was safe. God Himself had shut the door.

When the water finally went down and Noah stepped onto dry ground, the first thing he did was build an altar and worship God. Then God made a covenant, a solemn promise, with Noah and with every living creature: never again would a flood destroy the whole earth. The sign of the promise was the rainbow.
God takes sin seriously, because it destroys the people He loves. But God always makes a way of rescue too. The ark is a picture of Jesus: everyone who is in Him is safe.

verse.text: I have put my rainbow in the clouds. It is the sign of my promise.

lessons: God takes sin seriously because He loves people and sin destroys them.
Faith means trusting what God says even when you can’t see it yet.
God always keeps His promises, and He always makes a way of rescue.
questions: How long did Noah work on the ark? What do you think people said to him?
How is the ark like Jesus?
Is there something God has promised that you find hard to believe right now?
en.listen: Sit still and picture a rainbow. Ask God: ‘Which of your promises do you want me to remember this week?’ Write down anything that comes to mind, and check it in the Bible with your parent.
prayer: God, you always keep your promises.
Help me to trust you like Noah did, even when…
Thank you that I am safe in Jesus.

mission.text: Make a promise tomorrow and keep it, even if it’s hard. Remember that God keeps every promise.

en.journal: Draw a rainbow. On each colour, write one of God’s promises from the Bible (ask your parent to help you find some).

af.title: Die Ark en die Reënboog
story: Teen Noag se tyd het die wêreld ’n verskriklike plek geword. Die Bybel sê mense se gedagtes was ‘altyd net sleg’. Daar was oral geweld. Dit het God bedroef, wat beteken dit het sy hart seergemaak, dat die mense wat Hy gemaak het so ver van Hom af weggedraai het.

Maar Noag het ‘genade gevind in die oë van die Here’. Noag het met God gewandel. Toe het God vir Noag sy plan vertel: ’n vloed sou die aarde bedek, maar Noag, sy familie en twee van elke soort dier sou veilig gehou word in ’n reusagtige boot wat ’n ark genoem word. God het presiese mates gegee: omtrent 135 meter lank, 22 meter breed en 13 meter hoog.

Die Bybel sê: ‘Noag het alles gedoen net soos God hom beveel het.’ Om die ark te bou het jare gevat. Daar was geen reën in sig nie, en mense het seker gedink Noag het sy verstand verloor. Maar Noag het meer vertrou op wat God gesê het as op wat hy kon sien. Dit is wat geloof is.
Toe die vloed kom, het dit veertig dae en veertig nagte gereën, en die water het selfs die berge bedek. Maar binne-in die ark was almal veilig. God self het die deur toegemaak.

Toe die water eindelik gesak het en Noag op droë grond uitgestap het, was die eerste ding wat hy gedoen het om ’n altaar te bou en God te aanbid. Toe het God ’n verbond, ’n plegtige belofte, met Noag en met elke lewende wese gemaak: nooit weer sou ’n vloed die hele aarde vernietig nie. Die teken van die belofte was die reënboog.
God neem sonde ernstig op, want dit vernietig die mense vir wie Hy liefhet. Maar God maak ook altyd ’n pad van redding. Die ark is ’n prentjie van Jesus: almal wat in Hom is, is veilig.

verse.text: Ek het my reënboog in die wolke gesit. Dit is die teken van my belofte.

lessons: God neem sonde ernstig op omdat Hy mense liefhet en sonde hulle vernietig.
Geloof beteken om te vertrou wat God sê, selfs as jy dit nog nie kan sien nie.
God hou altyd sy beloftes, en Hy maak altyd ’n pad van redding.
questions: Hoe lank het Noag aan die ark gewerk? Wat dink jy het mense vir hom gesê?
Hoe is die ark soos Jesus?
Is daar iets wat God belowe het wat jy nou moeilik vind om te glo?
af.listen: Sit stil en stel jou ’n reënboog voor. Vra God: ‘Watter van u beloftes wil U hê moet ek hierdie week onthou?’ Skryf neer wat ook al opkom, en kyk saam met jou ouer in die Bybel daarna.
prayer: God, U hou altyd u beloftes.
Help my om U te vertrou soos Noag, selfs as…
Dankie dat ek veilig is in Jesus.

mission.text: Maak môre ’n belofte en hou dit, selfs al is dit moeilik. Onthou dat God elke belofte hou.

af.journal: Teken ’n reënboog. Skryf op elke kleur een van God se beloftes uit die Bybel (vra jou ouer om jou te help om ’n paar te kry).

trait.en: God always keeps his promises
trait.af: God hou altyd sy beloftes

en.title: Count the Stars
story: Abraham and his wife Sarah were very old, older than great-grandparents! And they had no children. They wished and wished for a baby.

One night God took Abraham outside. ‘Look up at the sky,’ God said. ‘Count the stars, if you can.’ Abraham looked up. One, two, three… hundreds… thousands! There were far too many to count. ‘Your family will be like that,’ God said. ‘Too many to count.’

Abraham thought, ‘How can that happen? We are too old!’ But Abraham believed God. And guess what? When Abraham was 100 years old, baby Isaac was born! Sarah laughed and laughed with happiness. Isaac’s name even means ‘he laughs’.
God can do what no one else can do. Nothing is too hard for him.

verse.text: Nothing is too hard for you.

lessons: Nothing is too hard for God.
God hears the wishes and prayers of our hearts.
Sometimes we have to wait, but God never forgets.
questions: What is something that seems too hard for you? Is it too hard for God?
How many stars do you think there are? (God knows every one!)
prayer: Dear God,
you made all the stars and you know how many there are.
Nothing is too hard for you.
Help me trust you with big things. Amen.

mission.text: Look at the stars with Mom and thank God for being so big.

af.title: Tel die Sterre
story: Abraham en sy vrou Sara was baie oud, ouer as oupagrootjies! En hulle het geen kinders gehad nie. Hulle het gewens en gewens vir ’n baba.

Een nag het God Abraham na buite geneem. ‘Kyk op na die hemel,’ het God gesê. ‘Tel die sterre, as jy kan.’ Abraham het opgekyk. Een, twee, drie… honderde… duisende! Daar was te veel om te tel. ‘Jou familie sal so wees,’ het God gesê. ‘Te veel om te tel.’

Abraham het gedink: ‘Hoe kan dit gebeur? Ons is te oud!’ Maar Abraham het God geglo. En raai wat? Toe Abraham 100 jaar oud was, is baba Isak gebore! Sara het gelag en gelag van blydskap. Isak se naam beteken selfs ‘hy lag’.
God kan doen wat niemand anders kan doen nie. Niks is te moeilik vir Hom nie.

verse.text: Niks is vir U te moeilik nie.

lessons: Niks is te moeilik vir God nie.
God hoor die wense en gebede van ons harte.
Soms moet ons wag, maar God vergeet nooit nie.
questions: Wat lyk vir jou te moeilik? Is dit te moeilik vir God?
Hoeveel sterre dink jy is daar? (God ken elkeen!)
prayer: Liewe God,
U het al die sterre gemaak en U weet hoeveel daar is.
Niks is vir U te moeilik nie.
Help my om U met groot dinge te vertrou. Amen.

mission.text: Kyk saam met Mamma na die sterre en dank God dat Hy so groot is.

en.title: So Many Stars
story: Abraham and Sarah wanted a baby very much.
One night God said, ‘Abraham, look up! Count the stars!’
One, two, three… so many! Too many to count!
God said, ‘Your family will be big, like the stars.’
Abraham believed God. And baby Isaac was born! Sarah laughed and laughed. Nothing is too hard for God.

verse.text: Nothing is too hard for God.

en.action: Twinkle your fingers like stars above your head, then count to three together.
lessons: God is so big. Nothing is too hard for Him.
questions: Can you see the stars tonight? Who made them?
prayer: Dear God,
you are so big and strong. Amen.

af.title: Soveel Sterre
story: Abraham en Sara wou baie graag ’n baba hê.
Een nag het God gesê: ‘Abraham, kyk op! Tel die sterre!’
Een, twee, drie… soveel! Te veel om te tel!
God het gesê: ‘Jou familie sal groot wees, soos die sterre.’
Abraham het God geglo. En baba Isak is gebore! Sara het gelag en gelag. Niks is vir God te moeilik nie.

verse.text: Niks is vir God te moeilik nie.

af.action: Laat jou vingers soos sterre bo jou kop vonkel, en tel dan saam tot drie.
lessons: God is so groot. Niks is vir Hom te moeilik nie.
questions: Kan jy vanaand die sterre sien? Wie het hulle gemaak?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is so groot en sterk. Amen.

en.title: Counting Stars
story: Abram (later renamed Abraham) was 75 years old when God told him to leave his home and go to a land God would show him. God promised to make him into a great nation. Abram went. But years passed, and Abram and his wife Sarai still had no children.

One night God spoke to Abram in a vision: ‘Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.’ Abram was honest with God: ‘What can you give me, since I have no child?’ God didn’t get cross with Abram for asking. Instead He took him outside. ‘Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you can. So shall your offspring be.’

Then comes one of the most important verses in the whole Bible: ‘Abram believed the Lord, and He credited it to him as righteousness.’ Abram didn’t earn God’s approval by being good enough. He simply believed what God said, and God counted him as right with Him. That is how it still works today: we are made right with God by faith, by trusting Jesus.

Believing wasn’t always easy. Abram and Sarai made mistakes while they waited. But God was faithful. When Abraham was 100 and Sarah was 90, she gave birth to a son. They named him Isaac, which means ‘he laughs’. Sarah said, ‘God has brought me laughter.’
Faith means taking God at His word. God speaks, we believe Him, and we keep trusting Him while we wait. Nothing is too hard for the God who made the stars.

verse.text: Abram believed the Lord, and the Lord counted it to him as righteousness.

lessons: Nothing is too hard for God.
We are made right with God by believing Him (faith), not by earning it.
It’s okay to be honest with God about our questions while we wait for His promises.
questions: What did God show Abram to help him believe?
What does it mean that Abram’s faith was ‘credited to him as righteousness’?
What are you waiting and praying for? How can you keep trusting God while you wait?
en.listen: If you can, look out of a window at the night sky. Ask God: ‘What do you want me to trust you for?’ Be still and listen. Share what you sense with your parent.
prayer: God, nothing is too hard for you.
I believe you, and I want to trust you with…
Thank you that I am right with you because of Jesus.

mission.text: Write down one thing you are trusting God for, and put it somewhere you will see it every day this week.

en.journal: Write about a time you had to wait for something. What helped? What does Abraham’s story teach you about waiting on God?

af.title: Sterre Tel
story: Abram (later het God sy naam na Abraham verander) was 75 jaar oud toe God vir hom gesê het om sy huis te verlaat en na ’n land te gaan wat God vir hom sou wys. God het belowe om ’n groot nasie van hom te maak. Abram het gegaan. Maar jare het verbygegaan, en Abram en sy vrou Sarai het steeds geen kinders gehad nie.

Een nag het God in ’n visioen met Abram gepraat: ‘Moenie bang wees nie, Abram. Ek is jou skild, jou baie groot beloning.’ Abram was eerlik met God: ‘Wat kan U my gee, want ek het geen kind nie?’ God was nie kwaad vir Abram omdat hy gevra het nie. Hy het hom eerder na buite geneem. ‘Kyk op na die hemel en tel die sterre, as jy kan. So baie sal jou nakomelinge wees.’

Dan kom een van die belangrikste verse in die hele Bybel: ‘Abram het die Here geglo, en Hy het dit vir hom as geregtigheid gereken.’ Abram het nie God se goedkeuring verdien deur goed genoeg te wees nie. Hy het eenvoudig geglo wat God gesê het, en God het hom as reg met Hom gereken. So werk dit vandag nog: ons word reg met God deur geloof, deur Jesus te vertrou.

Om te glo was nie altyd maklik nie. Abram en Sarai het foute gemaak terwyl hulle gewag het. Maar God was getrou. Toe Abraham 100 was en Sara 90, het sy ’n seun in die wêreld gebring. Hulle het hom Isak genoem, wat ‘hy lag’ beteken. Sara het gesê: ‘God het my laat lag.’
Geloof beteken om God op sy woord te neem. God praat, ons glo Hom, en ons hou aan om Hom te vertrou terwyl ons wag. Niks is te moeilik vir die God wat die sterre gemaak het nie.

verse.text: Abram het die Here geglo, en die Here het dit vir hom as geregtigheid gereken.

lessons: Niks is vir God te moeilik nie.
Ons word reg met God deur Hom te glo (geloof), nie deur dit te verdien nie.
Dit is reg om eerlik met God te wees oor ons vrae terwyl ons op sy beloftes wag.
questions: Wat het God vir Abram gewys om hom te help glo?
Wat beteken dit dat Abram se geloof ‘as geregtigheid gereken’ is?
Waarvoor wag en bid jy? Hoe kan jy aanhou om God te vertrou terwyl jy wag?
af.listen: As jy kan, kyk deur ’n venster na die naghemel. Vra God: ‘Waarvoor wil U hê moet ek U vertrou?’ Wees stil en luister. Vertel jou ouer wat jy aanvoel.
prayer: God, niks is vir U te moeilik nie.
Ek glo U, en ek wil U vertrou met…
Dankie dat ek reg is met U danksy Jesus.

mission.text: Skryf een ding neer waarvoor jy God vertrou, en sit dit êrens waar jy dit hierdie week elke dag sal sien.

af.journal: Skryf oor ’n keer toe jy vir iets moes wag. Wat het gehelp? Wat leer Abraham se storie jou oor om op God te wag?

trait.en: Nothing is too hard for God
trait.af: Niks is te moeilik vir God nie

en.title: Joseph's Colourful Coat
story: Joseph had eleven brothers, and his dad gave him a special, colourful coat. His brothers were so jealous that they did a very mean thing: they sold Joseph to traders, who took him far away to Egypt.

In Egypt more bad things happened. Joseph was even put in prison, though he had done nothing wrong. But the Bible says, ‘The Lord was with Joseph.’ Joseph kept doing what was right, and God helped him understand dreams.

One day the king of Egypt had a strange dream, and God helped Joseph explain it: seven years of plenty of food were coming, and then seven hungry years. The king made Joseph a great leader to store up food! When the hungry years came, Joseph’s brothers came to Egypt to buy food, and there was Joseph!
Joseph forgave them and hugged them. ‘You planned to hurt me,’ he said, ‘but God turned it into good.’

verse.text: You planned to harm me. But God planned it for good.

lessons: God is with us even when sad or unfair things happen.
God is in charge and can turn bad things into good things.
Joseph forgave his brothers, and God helps us forgive too.
questions: When was a time you felt sad or left out? Was God with you?
Is it easy or hard to forgive? Why?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you are with me
even when things are hard.
Help me forgive like Joseph did. Amen.

mission.text: Is there someone you need to forgive? Tomorrow, be extra kind to them.

af.title: Josef se Kleurryke Mantel
story: Josef het elf broers gehad, en sy pa het vir hom ’n spesiale, kleurryke mantel gegee. Sy broers was so jaloers dat hulle iets baie gemeens gedoen het: hulle het Josef aan handelaars verkoop, wat hom ver weg na Egipte geneem het.

In Egipte het nog slegte dinge gebeur. Josef is selfs in die tronk gegooi, al het hy niks verkeerd gedoen nie. Maar die Bybel sê: ‘Die Here was by Josef.’ Josef het aangehou om reg te doen, en God het hom gehelp om drome te verstaan.

Eendag het die koning van Egipte ’n vreemde droom gehad, en God het Josef gehelp om dit te verduidelik: sewe jaar met baie kos kom, en daarna sewe honger jare. Die koning het Josef ’n groot leier gemaak om kos op te gaar! Toe die honger jare kom, het Josef se broers na Egipte gekom om kos te koop, en daar was Josef!
Josef het hulle vergewe en hulle styf vasgedruk. ‘Julle het beplan om my seer te maak,’ het hy gesê, ‘maar God het dit in iets goeds verander.’

verse.text: Julle het kwaad teen my beplan, maar God het dit ten goede bedoel.

lessons: God is by ons, selfs as hartseer of onregverdige dinge gebeur.
God is in beheer en kan slegte dinge in goeie dinge verander.
Josef het sy broers vergewe, en God help ons ook om te vergewe.
questions: Wanneer het jy al hartseer of uitgelos gevoel? Was God by jou?
Is dit maklik of moeilik om te vergewe? Hoekom?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U by my is,
selfs as dinge moeilik is.
Help my om te vergewe soos Josef. Amen.

mission.text: Is daar iemand wat jy moet vergewe? Wees môre ekstra gaaf met hulle.

en.title: Joseph’s Coat
story: Joseph had a coat with lots of colours. Red, blue, yellow, green!
His brothers were cross. They sent Joseph far away.
But God was with Joseph all the time.
God helped Joseph, and Joseph became a big leader.
When his brothers came, Joseph gave them a big hug. ‘I forgive you,’ he said.

verse.text: God was with Joseph.

en.action: Point to all the colours you can find in your room. Then give someone a big hug, like Joseph.
lessons: God is with me, even when I am sad.
questions: What colour would your special coat be?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you are always with me. Amen.

af.title: Josef se Mantel
story: Josef het ’n mantel met baie kleure gehad. Rooi, blou, geel, groen!
Sy broers was kwaad. Hulle het Josef ver weg gestuur.
Maar God was die hele tyd by Josef.
God het Josef gehelp, en Josef het ’n groot leier geword.
Toe sy broers kom, het Josef hulle styf vasgedruk. ‘Ek vergewe julle,’ het hy gesê.

verse.text: God was by Josef.

af.action: Wys na al die kleure wat jy in jou kamer kan kry. Druk dan iemand styf vas, soos Josef.
lessons: God is by my, selfs as ek hartseer is.
questions: Watter kleur sou jou spesiale mantel wees?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U altyd by my is. Amen.

en.title: From the Pit to the Palace
story: Joseph was the second-youngest of twelve brothers and his father Jacob’s favourite. Jacob gave him a special robe, and Joseph had dreams in which his whole family bowed down to him. His brothers grew to hate him.

One day, far from home, the brothers grabbed Joseph, ripped off his robe and threw him into an empty well. Then they sold him to traders for twenty pieces of silver. Joseph was taken to Egypt as a slave.

In Egypt Joseph worked hard and did what was right, but things kept going wrong. He was falsely accused and thrown into prison for years. Yet again and again Genesis says, ‘The Lord was with Joseph.’ God was with him in the well, in the slave house and in the prison.

God gave Joseph the ability to understand dreams. When Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had dreams nobody could explain, Joseph was brought out of prison. ‘I cannot do it,’ Joseph said, ‘but God will give Pharaoh the answer.’ God showed that seven years of plenty would be followed by seven years of famine, and Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of all Egypt to prepare.

When the famine came, Joseph’s brothers travelled to Egypt to buy food and bowed before the governor without recognising him. Joseph could have taken revenge. Instead he wept, told them who he was and forgave them. ‘You intended to harm me,’ he said, ‘but God intended it for good, to save many lives.’

Joseph’s story shows that God is in charge even when life is unfair. He doesn’t cause the evil people do, but He can weave even the worst things into His good plan. And it shows that forgiveness is possible, because God helps us to forgive.

verse.text: You planned to harm me, but God planned it for good.

lessons: God is with His children in every hard place.
God is in charge, and He can turn even bad things into good.
With God’s help, we can forgive people who hurt us.
questions: How many times did life go wrong for Joseph? What stayed the same each time?
Why do you think Joseph chose to forgive instead of taking revenge?
Is there someone you find hard to forgive? What would it look like to forgive them?
en.listen: Sit quietly and ask God: ‘Where were you when things were hard for me?’ Listen for His answer. You might remember a moment when you felt His help. Thank Him for it.
prayer: God, thank you that you were with Joseph and you are with me.
Please help me to forgive…
I trust you to turn hard things into good.

mission.text: Do something kind tomorrow for someone who has upset you, just as Joseph did for his brothers.

en.journal: Draw Joseph’s journey: the well, the slave house, the prison, the palace. Next to each, write ‘God was with Joseph.’ Then add a place from your own life.

af.title: Van die Put tot die Paleis
story: Josef was die tweede jongste van twaalf broers en sy pa Jakob se gunsteling. Jakob het vir hom ’n spesiale mantel gegee, en Josef het drome gehad waarin sy hele familie voor hom gebuig het. Sy broers het hom begin haat.

Eendag, ver van die huis af, het die broers Josef gegryp, sy mantel afgeskeur en hom in ’n leë put gegooi. Toe het hulle hom vir twintig silwerstukke aan handelaars verkoop. Josef is as ’n slaaf na Egipte geneem.

In Egipte het Josef hard gewerk en reg gedoen, maar dinge het aanhou skeefloop. Hy is valslik beskuldig en jare lank in die tronk gegooi. Tog sê Genesis keer op keer: ‘Die Here was met Josef.’ God was by hom in die put, in die slawehuis en in die tronk.

God het Josef die vermoë gegee om drome te verstaan. Toe Farao, die koning van Egipte, drome gehad het wat niemand kon verklaar nie, is Josef uit die tronk gebring. ‘Ek kan dit nie doen nie,’ het Josef gesê, ‘maar God sal Farao die antwoord gee.’ God het gewys dat sewe jaar van oorvloed deur sewe jaar van hongersnood gevolg sou word, en Farao het Josef in beheer van die hele Egipte gesit om voor te berei.

Toe die hongersnood kom, het Josef se broers na Egipte gereis om kos te koop en voor die goewerneur gebuig sonder om hom te herken. Josef kon wraak geneem het. Hy het eerder gehuil, vir hulle vertel wie hy is en hulle vergewe. ‘Julle het beplan om my kwaad te doen,’ het hy gesê, ‘maar God het dit ten goede bedoel, om baie lewens te red.’

Josef se storie wys dat God in beheer is, selfs as die lewe onregverdig is. Hy veroorsaak nie die kwaad wat mense doen nie, maar Hy kan selfs die ergste dinge in sy goeie plan inweef. En dit wys dat vergifnis moontlik is, want God help ons om te vergewe.

verse.text: Julle het beplan om my kwaad te doen, maar God het dit ten goede bedoel.

lessons: God is by sy kinders op elke moeilike plek.
God is in beheer, en Hy kan selfs slegte dinge in iets goeds verander.
Met God se hulp kan ons mense vergewe wat ons seergemaak het.
questions: Hoeveel keer het dinge vir Josef skeefgeloop? Wat het elke keer dieselfde gebly?
Hoekom dink jy het Josef gekies om te vergewe in plaas van om wraak te neem?
Is daar iemand wat jy moeilik vind om te vergewe? Hoe sou dit lyk om hulle te vergewe?
af.listen: Sit stil en vra God: ‘Waar was U toe dinge vir my moeilik was?’ Luister na sy antwoord. Dalk onthou jy ’n oomblik toe jy sy hulp gevoel het. Dank Hom daarvoor.
prayer: God, dankie dat U by Josef was en dat U by my is.
Help my asseblief om te vergewe…
Ek vertrou U om moeilike dinge in goed te verander.

mission.text: Doen môre iets gaaf vir iemand wat jou ontstel het, net soos Josef vir sy broers gedoen het.

af.journal: Teken Josef se reis: die put, die slawehuis, die tronk, die paleis. Skryf langs elkeen: ‘God was met Josef.’ Voeg dan ’n plek uit jou eie lewe by.

trait.en: God is in charge and can turn bad into good
trait.af: God is in beheer en kan sleg in goed verander

story: You’ve finished your first expedition! af.title: Kampvuuraand: Die Skepper se Tuin
story: Jy het jou eerste ekspedisie klaargemaak! Hierdie week het jy gesien hoe God die heelal met sy woorde skep, mense na sy beeld maak, na Adam en Eva kom soek, Noag red, sy belofte aan Abraham hou en Josef se pyn in iets goeds verander. Kyk vanaand terug en sien wat jy ontdek het oor wie God is.
af.game: Skattevasvra: jou ouer lees ’n skat voor (byvoorbeeld ‘God is in beheer’), en jy noem die storie en een besonderheid daaruit. Ruil dan om: jy lees een voor en jou ouer antwoord!
questions: Watter skat oor God het jou hierdie week die meeste verras?
Wat het jy hierdie week die meeste gesien: God as Vader, Jesus, die Heilige Gees, God wat praat, of gehoorsaam omdat ons Hom liefhet?
Hoe het hierdie week die manier verander waarop jy met God praat?
prayer: God, U is my Skepper en my Vader.
Hierdie week het ek geleer dat U…
Dankie dat ek u kind is.

mission.text: Leer Genesis 1:1 uit jou kop en leer dit vir iemand in jou familie.

af.journal: Maak ’n skatkaart van hierdie ekspedisie: teken ses skatkiste en skryf in elkeen een ding wat jy oor God geleer het.

blurb.en: Baskets, burning bushes and a path through the sea. God rescues his people.

en.text: The Lord will fight for you. You only need to be still.

af.text: Die Here sal vir julle veg. Julle hoef net stil te wees.

en.title: A Basket on the River
story: In Egypt, a new king was afraid of God’s people, so he made a terrible rule: all the baby boys must be thrown into the river. One mum had a beautiful baby boy. She hid him for three months, but he kept getting bigger and louder!

So she made a little basket and covered it with sticky tar so it would float like a boat. She tucked her baby inside and set it in the tall grass by the river Nile. His big sister Miriam hid nearby to watch.

Who should come down to the river? The king’s own daughter, the princess! She heard the baby cry and felt sorry for him. ‘I will keep him,’ she said. Quick-thinking Miriam ran up: ‘Shall I find a lady to feed the baby for you?’ And she fetched… his very own mum!
The princess named him Moses. God had watched over that little basket every single second.

verse.text: The Lord will watch over your coming and going, now and forever.

lessons: God sees you and watches over you all the time, even while you sleep.
God can use anyone, even a big sister, to help with his plans.
God protects his people.
questions: Where do you need God to watch over you?
How did Miriam help?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you that you watch over me
when I’m awake and when I’m asleep.
I am safe in your hands. Amen.

mission.text: When you feel scared tomorrow, say, ‘God is watching over me.’

af.title: ’n Mandjie op die Rivier
story: In Egipte was ’n nuwe koning bang vir God se mense, en hy het ’n verskriklike reël gemaak: al die babaseuntjies moes in die rivier gegooi word. Een ma het ’n pragtige babaseuntjie gehad. Sy het hom drie maande lank weggesteek, maar hy het al hoe groter en harder geword!

Toe maak sy ’n mandjie en smeer dit met taai teer sodat dit soos ’n bootjie sou dryf. Sy het haar baba daarin toegemaak en dit in die lang riete langs die Nylrivier neergesit. Sy groot sussie Mirjam het naby weggekruip om te kyk.

En wie kom na die rivier? Die koning se eie dogter, die prinses! Sy het die baba hoor huil en jammer vir hom gevoel. ‘Ek sal hom hou,’ het sy gesê. Slim Mirjam het nader gehardloop: ‘Moet ek ’n vrou gaan soek om die baba vir u te voed?’ En sy het… sy eie ma gaan haal!
Die prinses het hom Moses genoem. God het elke enkele sekonde oor daardie mandjie gewaak.

verse.text: Die Here waak oor jou as jy kom en as jy gaan, nou en vir altyd.

lessons: God sien jou en waak heeltyd oor jou, selfs terwyl jy slaap.
God kan enigiemand gebruik, selfs ’n groot sussie, om met sy planne te help.
God beskerm sy mense.
questions: Waar het jy nodig dat God oor jou waak?
Hoe het Mirjam gehelp?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie dat U oor my waak
as ek wakker is en as ek slaap.
Ek is veilig in u hande. Amen.

mission.text: As jy môre bang voel, sê: ‘God waak oor my.’

af.deeper: Mirjam was dapper en slim. Hoe kan jy dapper en hulpvaardig wees vir jou familie?
af.journal: Skryf ’n dankie-briefie aan God omdat Hy oor jou waak.

trait.en: God watches over me
trait.af: God waak oor my

en.title: The Bush That Wouldn't Burn
story: Moses grew up and became a shepherd in the desert. One day, while looking after his sheep near a mountain, he saw something very strange: a bush on fire! The flames crackled and glowed, but the bush wasn’t burning up!
Moses went closer for a look. Then a voice came from the bush: ‘Moses! Moses!’ It was God! ‘Take off your sandals,’ God said, ‘because you are standing on holy ground.’

Holy means God is perfect and pure and completely special. There is no one like him. Moses hid his face. Then God said, ‘I have seen my people being hurt in Egypt. I have heard them crying. I am going to rescue them, and I am sending you.’
Moses asked, ‘What is your name?’ God answered, ‘I AM WHO I AM.’ God has always been, and always will be.

verse.text: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.

lessons: God is holy: perfect, pure and like no one else.
God sees and hears when his people are hurting.
God knows your name, just like he knew Moses’ name.
questions: Why do you think Moses took off his sandals?
How can we show God he is special to us? (Singing, praying quietly, listening.)
prayer: Holy God,
there is no one like you.
You are perfect and good.
Thank you that you know my name. Amen.

mission.text: Sing a song to God tomorrow, just for him.

af.title: Die Bos wat nie Uitbrand nie
story: Moses het grootgeword en ’n skaapwagter in die woestyn geword. Eendag, terwyl hy naby ’n berg na sy skape kyk, sien hy iets baie vreemds: ’n bos wat brand! Die vlamme het geknetter en gegloei, maar die bos het nie uitgebrand nie!
Moses het nader gegaan om te kyk. Toe kom ’n stem uit die bos: ‘Moses! Moses!’ Dit was God! ‘Trek jou sandale uit,’ het God gesê, ‘want jy staan op heilige grond.’

Heilig beteken God is volmaak en rein en heeltemal spesiaal. Daar is niemand soos Hy nie. Moses het sy gesig weggedraai. Toe sê God: ‘Ek het gesien hoe my mense in Egipte seergemaak word. Ek het hulle hoor huil. Ek gaan hulle red, en Ek stuur jou.’
Moses het gevra: ‘Wat is u naam?’ God het geantwoord: ‘EK IS WIE EK IS.’ God was nog altyd, en sal altyd wees.

verse.text: Heilig, heilig, heilig is die Here.

lessons: God is heilig: volmaak, rein en soos niemand anders nie.
God sien en hoor wanneer sy mense seerkry.
God ken jou naam, net soos Hy Moses se naam geken het.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het Moses sy sandale uitgetrek?
Hoe kan ons vir God wys dat Hy spesiaal is vir ons? (Sing, stil bid, luister.)
prayer: Heilige God,
daar is niemand soos U nie.
U is volmaak en goed.
Dankie dat U my naam ken. Amen.

mission.text: Sing môre ’n liedjie vir God, net vir Hom.

en.title: A Path Through the Sea
story: God sent Moses to the king of Egypt: ‘Let my people go!’ After many signs from God, the king finally said yes. Off went God’s people, thousands and thousands of them!

But then the king changed his mind. He sent his army with horses and chariots to chase them. God’s people came to the edge of the Red Sea. Water in front. An army behind. Nowhere to go! They were very scared.

Moses said, ‘Don’t be afraid! The Lord will fight for you.’ Moses held out his staff, and God sent a strong wind. WHOOOOSH! The sea split in two, with walls of water on each side and dry ground in the middle! God’s people walked right through to the other side.
When they were all safe, the water came crashing back down. God had rescued them! They sang and danced and praised their mighty God.

verse.text: The Lord will fight for you. You only need to be still.

lessons: God is mighty. Even the sea obeys him.
When we feel stuck, God can make a way.
God is a rescuer.
questions: What do you think it was like to walk between walls of water?
What makes you feel stuck or scared?
prayer: Mighty God,
you can do anything!
When I feel stuck,
help me trust you to make a way. Amen.

mission.text: Learn the sea action: hands together, then push them apart like the sea opening. Do it when you feel scared.

af.title: ’n Pad deur die See
story: God het Moses na die koning van Egipte gestuur: ‘Laat my volk gaan!’ Ná baie tekens van God het die koning uiteindelik ja gesê. Daar gaan God se mense, duisende en duisende van hulle!

Maar toe verander die koning van plan. Hy stuur sy leër met perde en strydwaens agter hulle aan. God se mense het by die Rooi See gekom. Water voor. ’n Leër agter. Nêrens om heen te gaan nie! Hulle was baie bang.

Moses het gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie! Die Here sal vir julle veg.’ Moses het sy staf uitgesteek, en God het ’n sterk wind gestuur. WOESJ! Die see het in twee gesplits, met mure van water aan elke kant en droë grond in die middel! God se mense het reg deur tot aan die ander kant gestap.
Toe almal veilig was, het die water teruggestort. God het hulle gered! Hulle het gesing en gedans en hulle magtige God geprys.

verse.text: Die Here sal vir julle veg. Julle hoef net stil te wees.

lessons: God is magtig. Selfs die see luister na Hom.
As ons vasgekeer voel, kan God ’n pad maak.
God is ’n Redder.
questions: Hoe dink jy was dit om tussen mure van water te loop?
Wat laat jou vasgekeer of bang voel?
prayer: Magtige God,
U kan enigiets doen!
As ek vasgekeer voel,
help my om U te vertrou om ’n pad te maak. Amen.

mission.text: Leer die see-aksie: hande saam, druk hulle dan uitmekaar soos die see wat oopgaan. Doen dit as jy bang voel.

story: God sent Moses to the king of Egypt: ‘Let my people go!’ After many signs from God, the king finally said yes. Off went God’s people, thousands and thousands of them!

But then the king changed his mind. He sent his army with horses and chariots to chase them. God’s people came to the edge of the Red Sea. Water in front. An army behind. Nowhere to go! They were very scared.

Moses said, ‘Don’t be afraid! The Lord will fight for you.’ Moses held out his staff, and God sent a strong wind. WHOOOOSH! The sea split in two, with walls of water on each side and dry ground in the middle! God’s people walked right through to the other side.
When they were all safe, the water came crashing back down. God had rescued them! They sang and danced and praised their mighty God.

verse.text: The Lord will fight for you. You only need to be still.

lessons: God is mighty. Even the sea obeys him.
When we feel stuck, God can make a way.
God is a rescuer.
questions: What do you think it was like to walk between walls of water?
What makes you feel stuck or scared?
prayer: Mighty God,
you can do anything!
When I feel stuck,
help me trust you to make a way. Amen.

mission.text: Learn the sea action: hands together, then push them apart like the sea opening. Do it when you feel scared.

en.fact: God led his people with a tall cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night. They never needed a map!
en.deeper: The people were stuck between the sea and an army. When do you sometimes feel stuck?
en.journal: Draw the walls of water and write Exodus 14:14 on the dry path in the middle.

af.title: ’n Pad deur die See
story: God het Moses na die koning van Egipte gestuur: ‘Laat my volk gaan!’ Ná baie tekens van God het die koning uiteindelik ja gesê. Daar gaan God se mense, duisende en duisende van hulle!

Maar toe verander die koning van plan. Hy stuur sy leër met perde en strydwaens agter hulle aan. God se mense het by die Rooi See gekom. Water voor. ’n Leër agter. Nêrens om heen te gaan nie! Hulle was baie bang.

Moses het gesê: ‘Moenie bang wees nie! Die Here sal vir julle veg.’ Moses het sy staf uitgesteek, en God het ’n sterk wind gestuur. WOESJ! Die see het in twee gesplits, met mure van water aan elke kant en droë grond in die middel! God se mense het reg deur tot aan die ander kant gestap.
Toe almal veilig was, het die water teruggestort. God het hulle gered! Hulle het gesing en gedans en hulle magtige God geprys.

verse.text: Die Here sal vir julle veg. Julle hoef net stil te wees.

lessons: God is magtig. Selfs die see luister na Hom.
As ons vasgekeer voel, kan God ’n pad maak.
God is ’n Redder.
questions: Hoe dink jy was dit om tussen mure van water te loop?
Wat laat jou vasgekeer of bang voel?
prayer: Magtige God,
U kan enigiets doen!
As ek vasgekeer voel,
help my om U te vertrou om ’n pad te maak. Amen.

mission.text: Leer die see-aksie: hande saam, druk hulle dan uitmekaar soos die see wat oopgaan. Doen dit as jy bang voel.

af.fact: God het sy mense bedags met ’n hoë wolk gelei en snags met ’n vuurkolom. Hulle het nooit ’n kaart nodig gehad nie!
af.deeper: Die mense was vasgekeer tussen die see en ’n leër. Wanneer voel jy soms vasgekeer?
af.journal: Teken die mure van water en skryf Eksodus 14:14 op die droë pad in die middel.

trait.en: God is mighty and he rescues
trait.af: God is magtig en Hy red

en.title: Bread from the Sky
story: After crossing the sea, God’s people walked into the desert. It was hot and sandy, and there were no shops, no farms and no food. Soon tummies were rumbling. ‘We’re hungry!’ the people grumbled.

God said, ‘I will rain down bread from heaven for you.’ The next morning, the ground was covered with little white flakes, like frost. ‘What is it?’ the people asked. In their language that sounds like ‘manna’, so that is what they called it! It tasted like biscuits made with honey. Yum!
Every morning God sent fresh manna, enough for everyone. In the evenings he sent birds called quail for meat. For forty years in the desert, God never once forgot to feed them.
God knows what we need, and he loves to take care of us.

verse.text: My God will meet all your needs.

lessons: God gives us what we need.
We can ask God for what we need, every day.
Instead of grumbling, we can say thank you.
questions: What are some things God gives you every day?
What could you say instead of grumbling?
prayer: Dear God,
thank you for my food,
my bed and my family.
You give me everything I need. Amen.

mission.text: Before every meal tomorrow, say a thank-you prayer.

af.title: Brood uit die Hemel
story: Ná die see het God se mense die woestyn in gestap. Dit was warm en sanderig, en daar was geen winkels, geen plase en geen kos nie. Gou het mae begin grom. ‘Ons is honger!’ het die mense gekla.

God het gesê: ‘Ek sal brood uit die hemel vir julle laat reën.’ Die volgende oggend was die grond vol klein wit vlokkies, soos ryp. ‘Wat is dit?’ het die mense gevra. In hulle taal klink dit soos ‘manna’, en dit is wat hulle dit genoem het! Dit het gesmaak soos koekies met heuning. Lekker!
Elke oggend het God vars manna gestuur, genoeg vir almal. Saans het Hy voëls gestuur, kwartels, vir vleis. Veertig jaar lank in die woestyn het God nie een keer vergeet om hulle kos te gee nie.
God weet wat ons nodig het, en Hy sorg graag vir ons.

verse.text: My God sal in al julle behoeftes voorsien.

lessons: God gee ons wat ons nodig het.
Ons kan God elke dag vra vir wat ons nodig het.
In plaas daarvan om te kla, kan ons dankie sê.
questions: Watter dinge gee God elke dag vir jou?
Wat kan jy sê in plaas daarvan om te kla?
prayer: Liewe God,
dankie vir my kos,
my bed en my familie.
U gee my alles wat ek nodig het. Amen.

mission.text: Sê môre voor elke ete ’n dankie-gebed.

trait.en: God gives me what I need

en.title: Rules from a Loving Father
story: God led his people to a big mountain called Mount Sinai. The mountain rumbled with thunder, lightning flashed, and a thick cloud covered the top. God called Moses to come up the mountain.

There God gave Moses ten special rules, written on two stone tablets. Love God most of all. Don’t make anything more important than God. Honour your mum and dad. Don’t steal. Don’t lie. Don’t want what belongs to others.

Why did God give rules? Not to spoil the fun! God’s rules are like the railing on a high bridge: they keep us safe. God is good, and his ways are always best for us. He gave the rules because he loves his people and wants them to live happily together.
Later, Jesus said all the rules fit into two: love God with all your heart, and love other people.

verse.text: Taste and see that the Lord is good.

lessons: God is good, and everything he tells us to do is good for us.
God’s rules show us how to love him and love others.
Obeying God is one way of loving him back.
questions: What rules does Mom have that keep you safe? Why does she make them?
Which of God’s rules is easy for you? Which one is hard?
prayer: Dear God,
you are good, and your ways are best.
Help me love you most of all
and love the people around me. Amen.

mission.text: Tomorrow, show God you love Him: say a happy ‘yes’ the first time you’re asked.

af.title: Reëls van ’n Liefdevolle Vader
story: God het sy mense na ’n groot berg gelei wat die berg Sinai genoem word. Die berg het gedreun van die donder, weerlig het geflits, en ’n dik wolk het die bopunt bedek. God het Moses geroep om op die berg te kom.

Daar het God vir Moses tien spesiale reëls gegee, op twee kliptafels geskryf. Het God die liefste van almal. Moenie enigiets belangriker as God maak nie. Eer jou ma en pa. Moenie steel nie. Moenie lieg nie. Moenie begeer wat aan ander behoort nie.

Hoekom het God reëls gegee? Nie om die pret te bederf nie! God se reëls is soos die reling op ’n hoë brug: hulle hou ons veilig. God is goed, en sy pad is altyd die beste vir ons. Hy het die reëls gegee omdat Hy sy kinders liefhet en wil hê hulle moet gelukkig saam lewe.
Later het Jesus gesê al die reëls pas in twee: het God lief met jou hele hart, en het ander mense lief.

verse.text: Proe en sien dat die Here goed is.

lessons: God is goed, en alles wat Hy vir ons sê om te doen, is goed vir ons.
God se reëls wys ons hoe om Hom en ander lief te hê.
Om God te gehoorsaam is een manier om Hom terug lief te hê.
questions: Watter reëls het Mamma wat jou veilig hou? Hoekom maak sy hulle?
Watter een van God se reëls is maklik vir jou? Watter een is moeilik?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is goed, en u pad is die beste.
Help my om U die liefste van almal te hê
en die mense rondom my lief te hê. Amen.

mission.text: Wys môre vir God jy is lief vir Hom: sê die eerste keer bly ‘ja’ as jy gevra word.

af.journal: Skryf die twee grootste reëls wat Jesus gegee het: het God lief en het ander lief. Teken ’n hart om hulle.

en.title: The Wall That Fell Down
story: After forty years, God’s people finally reached the land God had promised them. Their new leader was Joshua. But in the way stood the city of Jericho, with huge, thick walls and gates shut tight.
God gave Joshua a very unusual plan: ‘March around the city once a day for six days. Don’t say a word. On the seventh day, march around seven times. Then blow the trumpets and shout!’

That sounded strange! Who knocks down walls by walking? But Joshua and the people trusted God. Day one: march, march, march. Day two… Day six… Then on day seven, around and around they went, seven times. The priests blew their trumpets, TOOOOOT! And everyone shouted as loud as they could.
CRASH! The great walls tumbled down flat! God had done exactly what he said.

verse.text: Trust in the Lord with all your heart.

lessons: God can be trusted, even when his plan seems strange.
Obeying God brings big victories.
God does what he says he will do.
questions: Why do you think God asked them to march quietly?
Who do you trust most? Why?
prayer: Dear God,
I trust you with all my heart.
Even when I don’t understand,
help me obey you. Amen.

mission.text: March around your bed seven times tomorrow night, then shout, ‘God can be trusted!’

af.title: Die Muur wat Omgeval Het
story: Ná veertig jaar het God se mense eindelik by die land gekom wat God aan hulle belowe het. Hulle nuwe leier was Josua. Maar in die pad was die stad Jerigo, met groot, dik mure en hekke wat styf toe was.

God het vir Josua ’n baie snaakse plan gegee: ‘Marsjeer ses dae lank een keer per dag om die stad. Moenie ’n woord sê nie. Op die sewende dag, marsjeer sewe keer om. Blaas dan die trompette en skree!’

Dit het vreemd geklink! Wie slaan mure plat deur te loop? Maar Josua en die mense het God vertrou. Dag een: marsjeer, marsjeer, marsjeer. Dag twee… Dag ses… Toe op dag sewe, om en om het hulle gegaan, sewe keer. Die priesters het hulle trompette geblaas, TOETOEEET! En almal het so hard as hulle kon geskree.
KRAAAK! Die groot mure het platgeval! God het presies gedoen wat Hy gesê het.

verse.text: Vertrou op die Here met jou hele hart.

lessons: God kan vertrou word, selfs as sy plan vreemd lyk.
Om God te gehoorsaam bring groot oorwinnings.
God doen wat Hy sê Hy sal doen.
questions: Hoekom dink jy het God hulle gevra om stil te marsjeer?
Wie vertrou jy die meeste? Hoekom?
prayer: Liewe God,
ek vertrou U met my hele hart.
Selfs as ek nie verstaan nie,
help my om U te gehoorsaam. Amen.

mission.text: Marsjeer môreaand sewe keer om jou bed en skree dan: ‘God kan vertrou word!’

en.title: Campfire Night: The Great Rescue Road
story: What a road we have travelled! A baby in a basket, a burning bush, a sea that opened and walls that fell. Tonight we sit by the fire and remember how God rescues his people.
questions: Which rescue was the most exciting?
Has God ever helped you when you were scared?
prayer: Dear God,
you are my Protector and my Provider.
You are holy, mighty and good.
I can trust you. Amen.

mission.text: Say this week’s Treasure Verse with the sea action.

en.game: Rescue Road retell: Mom says a clue (basket, fire, sea, bread, trumpet). You shout which story it is and one thing it shows about God.

questions: Watter redding was die opwindendste?
Het God jou al gehelp toe jy bang was?
prayer: Liewe God,
U is my Beskermer en my Voorsiener.
U is heilig, magtig en goed.
Ek kan U vertrou. Amen.

mission.text: Sê hierdie week se Skatvers saam met die see-aksie.
